blocks.prompt: 10 If \(\frac{b + c - a}{a}, \frac{c + a - b}{b}, \frac{a + b - c}{c}\) are in A.P., show that \(a, b, c\) are in H.P.
blocks.explanation:
Proof wala sawal. Aakhir mein humein yeh dikhana hai ke \(\frac{1}{a}, \frac{1}{b}, \frac{1}{c}\) A.P. mein hain, kyunke tab hi \(a, b, c\) H.P. mein honge.
Is ki chaabi ek chhoti si trick hai: A.P. ki har term mein ek hi number jor dein to woh A.P. hi rehti hai.
Plan: har term mein 2 jorein, upar \(a + b + c\) ban jayega; phir us se divide kar dein.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\frac{b + c - a}{a}, \frac{c + a - b}{b}, \frac{a + b - c}{c}\) A.P. mein hain.
Saabit karna hai: \(a, b, c\) H.P. mein hain.
Tareeqa: Do qawaneen: (1) A.P. ki har term mein same number jorne se A.P. qaim rehti hai. (2) Har term ko same non-zero number se divide karne se bhi A.P. qaim rehti hai.

Har term mein 2 jorein
\[\dfrac{b + c - a}{a} + 2 = \dfrac{a + b + c}{a}\]
\[\dfrac{c + a - b}{b} + 2 = \dfrac{a + b + c}{b}\]
\[\dfrac{a + b - c}{c} + 2 = \dfrac{a + b + c}{c}\]
Kyun: Pehli term mein \(2 = \frac{2a}{a}\) likha, to upar \(b + c - a + 2a = a + b + c\). Har term ke upar ek letter minus tha; 2 guna wahi letter jorne se woh plus ban gaya. Teeno terms ka upar wala hissa ek jaisa ho gaya, yahi is trick ka kamaal hai.
Dhyan dein: 2 hi kyun? Kyunke 1 jorne se minus wala letter sirf khatam hota, plus nahi banta; 2 se upar poora \(a + b + c\) banta hai.

Yeh nayi terms A.P. mein hain
\[\dfrac{a + b + c}{a}, \; \dfrac{a + b + c}{b}, \; \dfrac{a + b + c}{c}\]
Kyun: Har term 2 se khisak gayi, lekin terms ke darmiyan farq wahi raha, is liye A.P. barqarar.

\(a + b + c\) se divide karein
\[\dfrac{1}{a}, \; \dfrac{1}{b}, \; \dfrac{1}{c} \text{ A.P. mein hain}\]
Kyun: Har term ko same number se divide karne se common difference bhi usi se divide hota hai, magar barabar hi rehta hai. Yeh tab jaiz hai jab \(a + b + c \ne 0\), jo hum maan lete hain.

Nateeja
Kyun: \(a, b, c\) ke reciprocals A.P. mein aa gaye, to H.P. ki definition ke mutabiq \(a, b, c\) H.P. mein hain.

Tasdeeq numbers se: \(a = 1, b = \frac{1}{2}, c = \frac{1}{3}\) lein (yeh H.P. hai, kyunke 1, 2, 3 A.P. hai). Di hui terms banti hain \(-\frac{1}{6}, \frac{5}{3}, \frac{7}{2}\), jin mein farq \(\frac{11}{6}\) aur \(\frac{11}{6}\) hai \(\checkmark\). Yani baat numbers par bhi sahi baithti hai.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(a, b, c\) H.P. mein hain.
